config.title: Build typed notification payloads

intro.title: Build typed notification payloads
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple notification system using TypeScript. You will create typed objects to represent different notification payloads, such as success, error, and warning messages. The core concept is using TypeScript's type annotations to define the shape and allowed properties of these payloads. You will work with interfaces and type aliases to ensure your data is structured correctly. By the end, you'll have a set of reusable, type-safe notification objects ready for use in an application.
intro.usecase: Typed notification payloads are essential in modern applications where different notification types require structured data. In e-commerce dashboards, order confirmations need product details and tracking numbers, while security alerts require timestamps and severity levels. Messaging apps use typed payloads to distinguish between text messages, file uploads, and system notifications, each with different required fields. This pattern ensures notifications are validated at compile time, preventing runtime errors when displaying critical information to users.

objectives: Construct TypeScript interfaces to define notification payload structures
Implement type-safe functions that generate notification payloads
Apply union types to handle different notification categories
Configure optional properties for flexible payload variations
Initialize typed notification objects with required and optional fields
Manipulate payload data while maintaining type safety
Integrate payload types with notification display components

steps.title: Import TypeScript type utilities
steps.instruction: Import the necessary TypeScript type utilities that will be used throughout the lesson. Add the import statement at the top of your file.
steps.hint: You'll need to import utilities for creating types. Use the 'type' keyword for imports.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing type utilities
import { SomeType, AnotherType } from './types';
steps.expectedOutcome: Your file will have the proper imports to start building typed notification payloads.
successCriteria: The import statement for TypeScript type utilities is added at the top of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an import, but make sure it's for the type utilities needed for notification payloads.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Check that you're importing the proper type utilities.

steps.title: Define the base Notification interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'Notification' with three properties: 'id' (string), 'title' (string), and 'message' (string).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.seedCode:
// Import TypeScript type utilities here

// Define the Notification interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a Notification interface that defines the basic structure for notification payloads.
successCriteria: The Notification interface is defined with id, title, and message properties, all typed as strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure all three properties (id, title, message) are defined with string types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Notification interface is missing or incorrect. Check that you used the 'interface' keyword and defined all required properties with string types.

steps.title: Create a union type for notification types
steps.instruction: Define a union type named 'NotificationType' with the literal string values 'info', 'warning', 'error', and 'success'.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword followed by the type name, an equals sign, and the union of string literals separated by the pipe (|) operator.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: union type for status values
type Status = 'pending' | 'active' | 'completed';
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationType union type is created with the four specified string literal values.
successCriteria: The NotificationType union type is defined with the values 'info', 'warning', 'error', and 'success'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your NotificationType includes all four string literal values: 'info', 'warning', 'error', and 'success'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Please define a union type called NotificationType with the values 'info', 'warning', 'error', and 'success'.

steps.title: Extend the Notification interface with type property
steps.instruction: Extend the existing Notification interface to include a 'type' property with the type NotificationType.
steps.hint: Add a new property declaration inside the interface. Remember to use the union type you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Notification interface now has a 'type' property of type NotificationType, making it more specific.
successCriteria: The Notification interface includes a 'type' property with the type NotificationType.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the 'type' property with the correct NotificationType type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Notification interface should include a 'type' property of type NotificationType. Check your syntax.

steps.title: Create a typed notification payload function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'createNotification' that takes parameters for id, message, and type, and returns a Notification object.
steps.hint: Define a function with three parameters: id (string), message (string), and type (NotificationType). The function should return an object matching the Notification interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createNotification is defined with proper parameter types and returns a typed Notification object.
successCriteria: The createNotification function exists, accepts three typed parameters (id: string, message: string, type: NotificationType), and returns a Notification object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function has all three parameters with correct types and returns a Notification object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't match the required signature. Check the parameter types and return type.

steps.title: Add type-specific properties using discriminated unions
steps.instruction: Create a discriminated union type called 'Notification' that includes type-specific properties: add a 'timeout' property for 'info' notifications and a 'priority' property for 'error' notifications.
steps.hint: Use the NotificationType union you created earlier to define separate interfaces for each notification type, then combine them into a union type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A discriminated union type 'Notification' that includes interfaces for 'info' with timeout, 'warning' with no extra properties, and 'error' with priority.
successCriteria: The Notification type is a discriminated union with separate interfaces for each NotificationType value, where 'info' has a timeout property and 'error' has a priority property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined separate interfaces for each notification type and combined them into a union type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The discriminated union type isn't quite right. Remember to create interfaces for each notification type with their specific properties, then combine them.

steps.title: Update the createNotification function with type guards
steps.instruction: Update the createNotification function to use type guards and return the appropriate notification type based on input.
steps.hint: You'll need to check the type property of the input object and return a notification object with the correct type-specific properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createNotification function should now properly handle different notification types with type-safe implementation.
successCriteria: The createNotification function uses type guards to check the notification type and returns the appropriate typed notification object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function properly checks the type property and returns the correct notification object with all required properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createNotification function doesn't yet use type guards properly. Review how to check the type property and return the appropriate notification object.

steps.title: Create a validation function for notification payloads
steps.instruction: Create a function named isValidNotification that takes an object parameter and returns a boolean, using a type predicate to check if the object matches the Notification type.
steps.hint: Use the 'is' keyword in the return type annotation to create a type predicate that validates the object's properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function isValidNotification that validates if an object is a valid Notification using TypeScript type predicates.
successCriteria: The isValidNotification function is defined with a type predicate return type and validates the object's id and message properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function uses the 'is' keyword in the return type and checks both id and message properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a function named isValidNotification that validates if an object has both id and message properties using a type predicate.

steps.title: Build a notification manager class
steps.instruction: Create a NotificationManager class with a private notifications array property typed as Notification[], and an addNotification method that takes a Notification parameter and pushes it to the array.
steps.hint: Define a class with a private property and a public method. Use proper TypeScript type annotations for the array and method parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationManager class with a typed notifications array and an addNotification method will be created, organizing notification logic in a class structure.
successCriteria: The NotificationManager class is defined with a private notifications: Notification[] property and a public addNotification(notification: Notification) method that adds to the array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the class, but make sure to include both the private notifications array (typed as Notification[]) and the addNotification method with a typed parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationManager class is missing or incomplete. Create a class with a private notifications: Notification[] property and an addNotification(notification: Notification) method.

steps.title: Test the typed notification system
steps.instruction: Create a test case that demonstrates type safety by attempting to pass incorrect data to the createNotification function.
steps.hint: Call createNotification with arguments that don't match the expected types for a specific notification type.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a type error test
const invalidTest = createNotification('info', { id: 123, message: 'Test' }); // id should be string
steps.expectedOutcome: The TypeScript compiler should show a type error when you pass incorrect data types to createNotification.
successCriteria: A test case is created that intentionally passes mismatched types to createNotification, demonstrating TypeScript's type safety.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a test, but it might not fully demonstrate type safety. Make sure you're passing clearly mismatched types (like a number where a string is expected).
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case doesn't demonstrate type safety. Try calling createNotification with arguments that violate the expected type definitions.
